chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Sailing to Europe in 1936 and starting at the Chez Florence
summary: Butler crossed on the Ile de France in a Teddy Bear coat and joined Willy Lewis at the small Chez Florence in Paris, bringing new Roberta music and the covered tone learned from Henry Walton.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That's kidding among professionals. So the band was a fun band. So when I went to Europe this was another experience again. So I arrived and I just bought a pretty plaid suit and at that time people wore balloon derbies; had pants: had a coat called a Teddy Bear coat. It was camel hair but it was big, like a teddy bear, I bought this coat (inaudible), Ile de France.
And we had a great trumpet player, he was with so and

so, and I had to do (inaudible). Wew, my goodness. But that cast was there, people talking that sweet stuff and drinking that champagne and stuff. I was there. Got sick, couldn't make it for two days. Then I got to class and met the people, met everybody. And this place was called the Chez Florence,

By the way, Walton had worked in this place, this trumpet player I was telling you about, always asking questions. So he had briefed me a long time ago, exactly what to expect. So I got in there and it seemed a lot of trumpet players had been in there but couldn't fit. The place was a very small place and people that I'd see Rolls Royces and Spanish---- outside, the man on the door. People sitting down and they're playing Viense waltzes and very soft music, but it was swinging.
(Inaudible). Trombone player, he was playing (inaudible). And the walls are sort of draped. Cats had full dress suits on. I thought of Noble Sissle (PHONETIC) then. (Inaudible).
The band reminds you of Noble Sissle?
Yeah. (Inaudible), I caught it right there. I said, well, Jack, now you've got to go in and play that thing with the covered tone. And I hit it right off.

I brought a whole thing of new music. I brought a---- this was 1936, '37 "Roberta" had come in. I brought all that music, you know. 'Fine Romance', and we'd put it up and (inaudible). I knew all the dynamics. (Inaudible). Rhythm and shading.
Oh, yeah, from when you were working in New Jersey.

Yeah, that (inaudible). Because, see, if she didn't like me, I wouldn't have no working papers. And she might get mad, I don't pay nothing back, cost too much money. So I said, 'Oh, Lordy!' I didn't know all that.
